audit_findings.title: Post-sale claim mismatch: FY2025 Pakistan earnings remain in the numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: $35 million FY2025 operating income; $17.85 million pre-tax ownership-step proxy (51% × $35 million); exact owner-earnings effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The historical owner-earnings anchor reflects the formerly consolidated Pakistan business, while the bridge and share claim are post-sale and include only a 20% retained interest.
audit_findings.evidence: We currently own 71 percent of the Pakistan business, whose financial results are consolidated and reported as part of All Other.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: ownership fell from 71% to 20% on June 30, 2026, but the $530.2 million anchor was not conformed. The filed operating-income scale is 6.6% of anchor, while the ownership-step proxy is 3.4%. Because operating income does not establish Pakistan's after-tax owner earnings, capital needs, or noncontrolling-interest treatment, the record cannot determine whether the valuation effect is material.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct FY2025 owner earnings excluding the disposed 51% claim, add only post-sale equity-method economics from the retained 20%, and verify that the $127 million post-deconsolidation cash proceeds and $65 million retained-interest value are represented exactly once in the June 2026 bridge.

audit_findings.title: The perimeter record conflates a Tate & Lyle acquisition with the Pakistan divestiture
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $3.5 billion acquisition consideration; up to approximately $4.2 billion additional indebtedness and approximately $6.0 billion total post-close indebtedness
audit_findings.mechanism: Tate & Lyle would add operating earnings and growth but also acquisition consideration, financing costs, debt, integration costs, and potentially new shares or other claims to the valuation perimeter and bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: T&HS faces competition globally from Archer-Daniels-Midland Company (“ADM”), Tate & Lyle, Cargill, and Roquette.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated record error: the stated acquisition is Tate & Lyle, whereas the supporting evidence describes the completed Pakistan sale. The acquisition consideration equals about 41% of the $8.52 billion base equity value, and potential additional debt equals about 49%, so the omitted transaction economics are plainly capable of changing the valuation conclusion. The acquisition remains pending, but presenting Pakistan-sale evidence as its perimeter support makes the current warning unreliable.
audit_findings.action: Create separate perimeter records for the completed Pakistan divestiture and pending Tate & Lyle acquisition. Reconcile the latter to Tate & Lyle earnings, assumed debt, cash used, financing and hedging costs, integration costs, synergies, and completion probabilities, then run distinct stand-alone and post-close valuations.

audit_findings.title: The $119 million stake add may double count equity-method businesses
audit_findings.magnitude: maximum identified bridge exposure $119 million, or $1.81 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Equity-method income enters owner earnings through Other operating income, while the investment value may also be added through stakes_net in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our share of the earnings or losses reported by equity method investees is recognized in Other operating income, net in the Consolidated Statements of Income, and we generally recognize our share of income or expense one month in arrears due to the timing of when results are available.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that equity-method earnings enter reported operating income, but the record does not identify which investments comprise stakes_net or whether their income was purged. Even if the entire $119 million add were duplicated and removed, bear and base values would be approximately $110.63 and $128.03 per share, still above the $101.26 market price; the adjusted 30% base buy-below level would be approximately $89.62, still below the market price. The maximum identified bridge exposure therefore does not change the valuation decision.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $119 million stake schedule by legal entity to the $201 million equity-method, $26 million equity, and $28 million marketable-security balances; document any earnings purge and remove any duplicated bridge amount.

audit_findings.title: Added cash may not all be distributable to common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $952 million added, or $14.51 per diluted share; $378 million held internationally ($374 million cash plus $4 million short-term investments); inaccessible or operationally required portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash and short-term investments dollar-for-dollar even though restricted, trapped, taxed, acquisition-committed, or operationally required cash is not distributable excess value.
audit_findings.evidence: Country capital controls, such as those imposed in Pakistan and Argentina, may prevent the repatriation of dividends or payments due to us from our investments and subsidiaries or transfer of consideration payments for divestitures, such our pending agreement to sell an interest in our Pakistan business, in countries that impose such controls.
audit_findings.explanation: Capital-control exposure is filed, but the affected amount is not disclosed. The full cash add is 11.2% of base equity value and exceeds the $11.18 per-share spread between bear value and market price; removing it entirely would reduce bear value to approximately $97.93 per share. Because even a substantial partial restriction or operating reserve could materially narrow the valuation range, this is reasonably capable of changing the conclusion despite the exact unavailable amount remaining unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30, 2026 cash ledger by jurisdiction and legal entity; identify restrictions, minimum operating cash, Pakistan-proceeds availability, repatriation taxes, and cash committed to Tate & Lyle; rerun the bridge using only verified distributable surplus cash.

audit_findings.title: A committed 25-year headquarters lease is absent from the historical earnings base
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $145 million construction-cost basis; net incremental recurring cost unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Future net occupancy expense would reduce owner earnings and terminal cash flow, or a measurable lease liability could enter the equity bridge when the lease commences.
audit_findings.evidence: Lease payments will be primarily based on the cost to construct the facility, which we estimate will be approximately $145 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The commitment is forward-looking: payments begin when the facility is ready, currently expected in the first half of 2028, and therefore are not in FY2025 owner earnings or the existing $181 million operating-lease liability. The $145 million figure is a construction-cost basis, not a payment schedule or present-value liability, and existing Bridgewater rent may be replaced. Present materiality cannot be established.
audit_findings.action: Monitor construction and commencement disclosures; obtain the payment schedule, discount rate, incentives, and terminating existing-facility rent, then incorporate only the net incremental after-tax recurring cost or recognized liability.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded retiree benefits are an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $59 million obligation, or $0.90 per diluted share; filed annual benefit payments of $4 million versus $5 million FY2025 periodic benefit cost
audit_findings.mechanism: A bridge deduction or incremental owner-earnings allowance would be needed only to the extent prior-service benefit payments are not already represented by recurring benefit expense.
audit_findings.evidence: Our postretirement benefit plans currently are not funded.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation is a filed senior claim, but current scale does not support materiality. A full $59 million bridge deduction would reduce bear and base values only to approximately $111.54 and $128.94 per share, and the adjusted buy-below level to approximately $90.26, leaving the valuation decision unchanged. Moreover, expected annual payments through 2030 are $4 million, below the $5 million expense already present in FY2025 earnings, so the record demonstrates no current incremental cash-flow shortfall.
audit_findings.action: Confirm that the $59 million liability remains recorded in current and non-current liabilities and monitor whether future cash payments materially exceed recurring expense; rerun only if an excess-payment stream develops.
